title: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)

Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director

About Everfield

Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions.

We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units.

The Opportunity

The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region.

This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them.

Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units.

How the Role Operates

• Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself.

• Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done.

• You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver.

• Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams.

What You Will Do

Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration

• Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth.

• Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number.

• Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster.

• Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation.

• Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention.

• Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction.

• Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability.

Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity

• Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better.

• Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews.

• Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag.

• Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter.

Revenue Standards & Definitions

• Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place.

• Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement.

• Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio.

Commercial Governance

• Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning.

• Support commission structure alignment with business goals.

• Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility.

Commercial Diagnostics

• Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost.

• Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date.

• Prioritise your own time across the cluster on distance to target, materiality to the region, and whether a documented plan already exists.

• Provide feedback on pricing discipline, discounting practices, packaging effectiveness, and ICP conversion efficiency.

• Translate performance signals into executive-level recommendations and commercial action plans.

CEO & General Director Partnership

• Act as strategic commercial partner to CEOs and Business Unit leaders, representing Everfield's revenue expectations and performance discipline.

• Challenge growth assumptions constructively and escalate persistent underperformance when required.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 12 months:

• Full visibility into the commercial funnel, aligned with HQ reporting standards.

• Acceleration of organic recurring revenue growth across the region.

• Improved reliability of pipeline data and forecast accuracy.

• Sales pipelines that more accurately predict bookings performance.

• At least one Business Unit where you hold sales management directly and the team delivers against its number.

• Reliable visibility of quota attainment and seller productivity.

• Deal reviews embedded across portfolio sales teams, resulting in higher win rates and shorter sales cycles.

• Revenue per seller increasing steadily across the cluster.

• A documented, reusable set of playbooks and diagnostics that other regions can apply without starting again.

What We Are Looking For

• 6-10 years total experience in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 3-4 years in a sales management position, accountable for a team's bookings performance and not only for personal pipeline contribution.

• Track record of consistent revenue target attainment in a management role. You have owned a number and delivered against it, not only improved process quality.

• Direct experience leading and developing a sales team, including hiring, coaching, and managing underperformance. You will do this again here, inside our Business Units.

• Track record of implementing structured pipeline management: defining stage criteria, enforcing qualification standards, running deal reviews, and improving forecast reliability.

• Experience diagnosing revenue performance across the full funnel: understanding where deals are lost, why cycles extend, and what structural issues limit growth.

• Manages through CRM data: uses pipeline data to run structured deal reviews, identify risk, and hold sellers accountable to data quality. Familiar with Salesforce or HubSpot as a management tool.

• Experience working with senior stakeholders (CEOs, founders, or general managers) on commercial performance, including navigating organisational resistance and earning trust before driving change.

• Experience adapting sales management approach across companies at different sales maturity levels: able to calibrate coaching, process rigour, and expectations to fit the context.

• German fluency required, with professional English for work across the group. European B2B SaaS market experience required.

• Commercial finance literacy is a strong advantage: reading a P&L, understanding revenue recognition, and being able to argue the return on a commercial investment.

• Private-equity-backed or multi-entity SaaS environment experience is a strong advantage.

Skills

• Structured coaching and seller development: designing and running structured 1:1s, deal reviews, and field accompaniment to build individual seller capability, not just inspect opportunities.

• Pipeline discipline and forecasting: reading a pipeline critically, identifying risk early, and improving forecast reliability.

• Change management: driving commercial process adoption across multiple teams, and building momentum without relying on formal authority.

• Documentation and knowledge scale: writing down what you diagnose and what you implement, in a form another person can pick up and run. Work that lives only in conversation does not scale across a portfolio, and anything you build for one Business Unit should be reusable in the next.

• Commercial planning and challenge: building a bottom-up view of what revenue targets are achievable, pressure-testing top-down assumptions, and presenting credible alternatives to leadership.

• Commercial storytelling: presenting clear, honest risk assessments to CEOs and senior leadership, and leading a review that drives decisions rather than just restating numbers.

  • Full Business proficiency in German and English is a must

Who You Are

• You lead teams and you influence without authority. You will manage sellers directly in some Business Units and hold no formal authority in others. Both need to work. You build trust quickly and drive change through credibility, clarity, and structured analysis.

• You are hands-on with sales execution. You are comfortable stepping into real deals, reviewing opportunities with sellers, and diagnosing pipeline issues directly with the team, without needing to be the person closing.

• You combine analytical thinking with practical commercial judgement. You interpret pipeline data, and you also understand the realities of getting deals done.

• You communicate clearly and directly. You raise commercial risks early, with a recommendation attached, and challenge assumptions constructively, including when performance doesn't meet expectations.

You are pragmatic in complex environments. Portfolio companies vary in maturity and commercial model. You bring discipline without imposing rigid process that doesn't fit the situation

Hiring Processs:

TA screen (30min)

Hiring Manager interview (90min)

Group Director interview

title: Solution Consulting Manager
descriptionHtml:
What We Do

Rillet serves accounting and finance teams, the financial brains of their companies. Our job is to help them run the numbers with impossible speed, accuracy, and insight.

Rillet is the Agentic ERP built for modern finance teams. We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 600 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG.

We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.

Who We Are

Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.

The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.

Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan.

Rillet is built on deep accounting expertise, and it takes people from many disciplines to build a category-defining company. You do not need to be an accountant to thrive here. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Together, we combine the precision of accounting with the speed, creativity, and ambition of AI-native software to power the financial core of the world’s fastest-growing companies while redefining what finance teams should expect from their software.

The Role

We have grown quickly, and our Solution Consulting team is at the center of how prospects evaluate Rillet as their next ERP. We are looking for a Solution Consulting Manager to lead and scale that team.

This is a player-coach role weighted heavily toward coaching. You will spend roughly 25% of your time running your own sales cycles (staying sharp, credible and close to the customer and product) and roughly 75% of your time coaching, mentoring and developing your team, primarily by riding shotgun on live deals and giving real-time feedback. You will also be a key voice in shaping the product and building the Solution Consulting infrastructure that lets the organization scale.

You will work directly with the CEO, GTM leadership and the Product team.

Responsibilities

Coach, mentor and develop the team (~75%)

  • Ride shotgun on deals. Join discovery calls, demos, technical validations and POCs to observe, step in when needed, and give specific, real-time feedback. Run tight pre-call prep and post-call debriefs so every deal is a learning opportunity.

  • Raise the bar on craft. Coach Solution Consultants on discovery, value selling, storytelling, demo design, handling technical objections, and tailoring sandbox environments to each customer's use cases.

  • Grow each person individually. Set clear expectations and development plans, give regular honest feedback, and help each Solution Consultant build deep product and accounting domain expertise and advance in their career.

  • Hire and onboard. Recruit, interview and ramp new Solution Consultants, and build an onboarding program that gets them deal-ready quickly.

  • Partner on deal strategy. Work with Account Executives and sales leadership to staff deals, pressure-test strategy on complex ERP evaluations, and keep technical wins on track.

Run your own sales cycles (~25%)

  • Remove technical objections. Take on strategic and complex opportunities, understanding the prospect's business requirements and existing technology stack, and clearly articulating how Rillet integrates and improves their processes.

  • Deliver high-impact demos. Set up and tailor the sandbox environment, answer questions in real time, and act as the prospect's trusted consultant throughout the purchase process.

  • Represent Rillet. Be the face of the company, applying high customer empathy and structured problem-solving to ensure every prospect interaction is excellent, including with finance and accounting leaders.

Inform product and build for scale

  • Be the voice of the prospect. Synthesize front-line feedback, objections, competitive intel and feature gaps from across the team, and bring it to founders and Product in close to real time, with clear patterns and prioritization.

  • Influence the roadmap. Partner with Product on discovery, early feedback on new features, and how capabilities are positioned and demoed.

  • Build Solution Consulting infrastructure. Create the systems, playbooks and tools that help the team scale, such as discovery frameworks, demo standards and reusable assets, sandbox and demo-data templates, technical FAQs and objection libraries, POC and technical-validation processes, a deal-review cadence, and enablement and certification paths.

  • Measure what matters. Define and track team metrics (technical win rate, ramp time, deal coverage, cycle time) and use them to improve how the team operates.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years managing or formally mentoring pre-sales, solutions consulting or sales engineering teams, with a track record of developing people.

  • 3+ years of industry accounting experience across areas such as revenue recognition, month-end close and multi-entity consolidation.

  • 3+ years supporting complex ERP sales cycles with implementation and/or customer support for accounting or financial solutions.

  • Deep knowledge of the ecosystem of tools in the office of the CFO.

  • Excellent communicator who makes complex concepts easy to understand, and who can give direct, constructive feedback in the moment.

  • Experience building processes, enablement or tooling for a growing team, ideally in an early-stage, fast-moving environment.

  • Thrives in a dynamic environment while keeping high attention to detail.

  • CPA certification or having started your career in audit is a plus.

Note: All official Rillet recruiting communications will come from an @rillet.com email address. If you’re contacted from another domain, please disregard the message and report it as spam.

Life at Rillet

  • Benefits that support you. We offer competitive benefits designed to support your health, wellbeing, time away from work, family, and long-term financial goals.

title: Research Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Location: Oxford or London (Hybrid)

The Mission: Why We Exist

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

 

Role Purpose

We're looking for an exceptional Research Engineer with strong computational skills and a track record of applying them to large-scale data science. A background in human genetics is preferred, but if you come from another quantitative field and are excited by the potential of genetics to transform healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.

You'll join a team of experts in human genetics, data science and software engineering, building the platform at the heart of our Life Sciences work – (1) helping us derive new insights into human biology and guide drug development towards safer, more effective targets; (2) providing our SaaS customers with innovative analytics. How your time splits across methodology, software engineering and analysis will reflect your own balance of computational and scientific strengths.

This role can be hired at IC2 (Research Engineer) or IC3 (Senior Research Engineer) level, depending on your experience. At IC3, you'll operate with greater autonomy, hold a broader technical scope, bring deeper subject-matter expertise, and lead projects that require integrated updates across multiple tools, working with cross-disciplinary teams to deliver value.

A Day in the Life

At the heart of this role is the opportunity to collaborate with domain experts at the cutting edge of statistical genetics and rapidly translate their innovations into a mature, integrated data & analytics engine for commercial use at scale.

  • Help expand and maintain our in-house Life Sciences tools and pipelines, planning your own work and contributing code to a shared codebase alongside Research Engineering team members, Software Engineers and Data Scientists.

  • Implement algorithms developed within our Life Sciences teams to a high standard of robustness, testing and performance.

  • Run high-quality analyses of large-scale biological datasets using existing or bespoke tools, and share your findings with scientists and other stakeholders.

  • Contribute to internal and external presentations and publications arising from our work.

  • Keep your knowledge current on innovation and good practice in genomics, data science and scientific computing.

  • At Senior (IC3) level, you'll also lead projects that need integrated updates across multiple tools, coordinating with cross-disciplinary teams to deliver value.

Who You Are

  • Experienced running tools and workflows in a scalable system, for example Linux based HPC environments or on cloud systems.

It'd be great if you also have

  • Experience working on a collaborative codebase using version control and CI/CD.

  • Experience designing and running large-scale workflows, e.g. WDL, CWL.

  • Experience working in remote, cloud-based environments, e.g. AWS.

  • Experience creating and working with containers, e.g. Docker, Singularity.

  • A PhD or postgraduate degree in a scientific field, ideally genomics, bioinformatics or computational biology, with familiarity in statistics and machine learning.

  • Prior experience working in a team, ideally in an industry setting.

title: Research Manager, Biodefense
descriptionHtml:
You support fellows in the Biodefense Fellowship, so that each one does strong work and moves into a role where they can reduce catastrophic biological risk.

  • Salary: £86,750–£121,500 per year. We may be able to pay more for exceptional candidates.

  • Location: London, at our office at LISA

  • Hours: Full time

  • Visa: We can sponsor a Skilled Worker visa, but approval isn't guaranteed.

Why work at Pivotal

Pivotal finds people who can work on the biggest risks from advanced AI and gets them working on them. AI and synthetic biology are making it easier to create dangerous pathogens, so in 2026 we started the Biodefense Fellowship, which focuses on defences such as early detection, protective equipment and medical countermeasures. Since 2024, 135 fellows have taken part in our fellowships, and alumni now work at METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI and GovAI. We have grown from 2 staff in 2024 to 10 today, and we plan to reach at least 16 in 2027. Read more about us at pivotal-research.org, and about what it is like to work here.

What you will own

You'll be the Research Manager for about 6 research fellows, supporting each project from scoping through to publication. You'll collaborate closely with our whole research management team.

You'll engage deeply with your fellows' work: reading drafts, questioning experimental designs, suggesting framings, and helping projects stay ambitious but tractable. You’ll also hold the thread that keeps projects moving and fellows well supported.

  • Your fellows. Regular check-ins, project planning, unblocking, and feedback on drafts.

  • Projects and mentors. Use your knowledge of the field to help find biodefense mentors and to judge which projects matter most.

  • Information hazards. Help fellows handle sensitive biological information responsibly, and decide with mentors what is safe to publish.

  • Career outcomes. Help fellows move into biosecurity organisations, government and policy roles.

  • Wellbeing. Look after your fellows' wellbeing, with support from our community manager.

  • Between cohorts. Help design the next cohort, and support other programs where needed.

Research management at Pivotal

As an individual researcher, you might advance one or two projects. In this role, you'll have a hand in about 6 projects simultaneously (and about 18 projects every year). Your leverage comes from making each fellow meaningfully more effective than they would be on their own.

The biodefense field has an extremely limited talent pipeline, and many of the people who will shape it over the next few years are early in their careers, still developing their research taste, and often short on high-quality guidance. This role sits at that bottleneck. You’ll help the next generation of researchers produce stronger work, find the right collaborators, and move into positions where they can have outsized impact.

If you get energy from seeing other people's work click into place, this role may let you shape the field more than you could as a single researcher.

Who does well in this role

  • A background in biosecurity research or policy.

  • You know the biosecurity field and its organisations, which helps with mentors and careers.

  • Good judgement about handling sensitive research information.

  • Strong project management across several projects at once.

  • Care for people: fellows trust you and tell you early when things go wrong.

  • You want to spend a large part of your career reducing catastrophic biological risk.

We don’t expect anyone to be strong in all of this. If the role excites you, please apply, even if you match only part of what we describe here.

How we hire

We review applications as they come in, so applying early helps. The process has these stages:

  • Written application. A short form and your CV. It takes about 30 minutes.

  • Automated video interview. About 10 minutes. You record short answers to a few questions, at a time that suits you.

  • Work task. About 2 hours, based on real work in this role. We pay you for this time. You may use AI tools, as you would in the job. Tell us which ones you used and how.

  • Personal interview. About 45 minutes. We discuss your work task and how you would approach the role. With your consent, we record it so that more of the team can review it.

  • Work trial and references. Up to three paid days working with us at our office in London. We also speak to two referees, after asking you.

If you need an adjustment at any stage, such as extra time, tell us and we will arrange it. If you have questions, email ----- £86,750 – £121,500

title: Scientist - Phenotypic Data
descriptionHtml:
Location: Oxford, London or RTP (Hybrid)

The Mission: Why We Exist

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

 

Role Purpose

Genetic analyses are only as good as the definitions of disease they’re built on. Get the phenotype wrong and everything downstream wobbles.

As a Scientist in Clinical Informatics, you’ll define, curate and validate phenotypes from electronic health records and other clinical data. That gives our genetic discovery work and risk tools foundations that are accurate, clinically meaningful and reproducible. You’ll join the Life Sciences team, which tackles challenges across the therapeutic development cycle, from target discovery to patient stratification and finding new opportunities for existing drugs.

This is an early-career role in a highly collaborative team. You’ll be supported to develop your own ownership of analyses, and you’ll see your work reused across projects.

A Day in the Life

  • Developing and validating phenotype definitions for diseases with unmet need, using coded and clinical data (diagnoses, procedures, prescriptions, laboratory measurements) and standard terminologies, and assessing their accuracy and potential sources of bias

  • Harmonising and characterising phenotypic data across cohorts and health data sources, describing disease onset, progression and treatment patterns to identify relevant patient populations and biomarkers

  • Applying and evaluating risk stratification tools that combine polygenic risk scores with conventional clinical risk factors, to find the people most at risk and those most likely to benefit from particular therapies

  • Contributing reusable, version-controlled phenotyping code, pipelines and methods that feed into our technology

  • Working with genetic analysts, data engineers and clinical advisers, and presenting your findings to scientific and clinical audiences

Who You Are

You’ll bring:

  • A PhD in a quantitative discipline (epidemiology, biostatistics, health data science, medical informatics or genetics, for example)

  • Solid foundations in statistics (modelling, regression)

  • Experience with clinical or health data, such as electronic health records, cohort or registry data

  • Statistical programming in Python or R

  • Clear spoken and written communication, the ability to manage your own objectives and deliver on time, and a team-player mindset that puts your work in the bigger picture

  • Comfort with large, complex, imperfect clinical datasets, and a scientist’s instinct for questions of data quality and validity

It’s a bonus if you have:

  • Experience defining phenotypes from EHRs, using coded data or free text

  • Familiarity with clinical terminologies and data models (ICD-10, SNOMED CT, OPCS-4, OMOP, HPO)

  • An understanding of epidemiological study design and bias (confounding, selection bias, measurement error)

  • Knowledge of survival or longitudinal modelling and causal inference

  • Familiarity with statistical genetics (GWAS, polygenic risk scores), genetics and molecular biology

  • Experience applying NLP or machine learning to clinical text or structured health data

  • SQL and software engineering practices (Git and GitHub, testing, documentation, agentic coding, containerisation)

  • Reproducible pipelines (WDL, Snakemake or Nextflow) and cloud or trusted research environments (DNAnexus, Verily Workbench)

 

Your Package

We are committed to providing a transparent, supportive, and rewarding work environment.

Compensation & Growth

  • Competitive Salary: Salaries are externally benchmarked annually to ensure competitive compensation.

  • Clear Career Path: A straightforward, open progression framework means you'll always know the path to promotion and how to achieve your next career goal.

  • Continuous Learning: Including external courses and a wide library of L&D materials, because your growth is our success.

Wellbeing & Time Off

  • Holiday: 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, plus an extra 3-day company-wide shutdown at year-end.

  • Financial & Health Security: Robust benefits including a market-leading pension scheme, comprehensive private health insurance for you and your family with NO excess, critical illness, and life assurance.

  • Enhanced Leave: Enhanced paid family leave to support all new parents.

Work Environment & Culture

  • Flexible Working: Hybrid Working (e.g., From our London, Oxford Office)

  • Truly Inclusive Time Off: Our 'Bank Your Bank Holiday' program allows you to exchange public holidays for dates that hold personal or cultural significance to you.

  • Vibrant Social Culture: From regular Town Halls and team picnics to organised sports events, our social committee ensures frequent opportunities to connect and celebrate.

  • Green Commute: Cycle-to-Work scheme and convenient office locations near major transport hubs.

Ready to Build the Future?

title: SDR/BDR
descriptionHtml:
SDR/BDR Hybrid, Paris
Location: Paris (in-office)
Type: Full-time
Team: Founding GTM Team

About the Role
We're hiring Linkup's first SDR/BDR, a hybrid pipeline-generation role covering both sides of the funnel: qualifying inbound signups and running structured outbound into our priority segments (AI-native companies, GTM tooling providers, enterprise and regulated accounts).
You'll work closely with our VP Sales, picking accounts, drafting outbound, and partnering with AEs to turn interest into qualified pipeline. High ownership, fast feedback loop.

What You'll Do

  • Research target accounts and draft personalized multi-channel outreach (email, LinkedIn, phone) for founder-led and AE-assisted outbound

  • Monitor and pre-qualify inbound signups against our ICP (AI-native, GTM tooling, enterprise), then route to the right AE

  • Support first-touch qualification alongside AEs, learning our lead framework (ICP fit, pain, volume, timing, right entry point) as you go

  • Keep every touch logged in Attio

  • Help tune outbound messaging and channels as we scale campaigns across segments


Why This Role Matters
This is the first dedicated pipeline-generation hire at Linkup. Get it right and it compounds into every AE's quota.

You're a Great Fit If You

  • Have 0 to 2 years in SDR/BDR, or a first job out of a fast-paced, competitive environment (sales, consulting, we care about drive more than tenure)

  • Are comfortable with high-volume outbound and don't wait to be told what to do

  • Write clean, direct, non-generic outreach, no template-speak

  • Are curious about AI/agents and can hold a real conversation with a technical buyer, even without an engineering background

  • Want ownership fast, this role works closely with sales leadership, not layers of management

Our Stack
Attio (CRM), LemList (outbound), Slack, Notion, Apollo/Sales Navigator (prospecting), Snitcher (visitor ID), RB2B

About Linkup
Our Vision

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web. These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting. The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up. We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup.

 

Our Mission

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

 

Our Culture

Our culture is built on the following values:

  • Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

  • Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

  • Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

  • Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

  • Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

 

Our Team

We are small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.

A bit more about our 3 co-founders:

  • Philippe Mizrahi- Led the development of Lyft’s Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen, an open source search engine.

  • Denis Charrier- Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience.

  • Boris Toledano- Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

title: Senior AI Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.

Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

Our ambition is to put AI capability in every worker’s hands. Apprenticeships got us started: we’ve trained over a third of the UK’s data and AI apprentices, worked with a third of the FTSE 100, and generated £2bn+ in verified ROI. Now Mastry, our new adaptive learning platform, takes that further, guiding a company’s AI workforce transformation from start to finish. Mae, our AI guide inside Mastry, is a real-time AI agent that thinks, speaks, listens and sees, working alongside the tools you already use, like Claude and Copilot.

We closed our latest fundraising round in April 2026, with $500m+ raised in total from VC partners including Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Schroders Capital and Lightspeed. With a $2.1bn valuation, we are Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn, and we are just getting started.

If you want to shape how the workforce wins in the AI era, come and join us.

Why this role exists

Every foundation model lab is solving the same problem: build more capability. Almost nobody is solving the harder one — what happens when that capability meets a real organisation and real people who have to relearn how they work. That's the adoption layer, still wide open, and Multiverse sits in the unique position to solve this problem with ten years of proprietary learner and employer data driven from 1,500+ companies that no one else has.

Diagnose & Prescribe (D&P) is the engine room of that problem. It works out what a learner or employer actually needs, then decides what they get funded for and which apprenticeship or learning path they're pointed to next. D&P is how we assess a learner's or employer's skill gaps, decide what they need, and point them to the right apprenticeship or learning path — so the blast radius here is human and financial, not just a dashboard metric.

The line between leading this team and building the product has already blurred, which is why this role exists as it does. We need a leader who stays close enough to the work to have credible judgment in it, and who builds a high-trust team where diverse perspectives actually make the problem-solving better.

This is a broad, domain-coherent, event-driven and increasingly AI-native estate. The dominant challenge isn't deep algorithmic difficulty in any single repo — it's holding the whole D&P picture, sequencing work across varied services, and keeping load-bearing decisions safe as the system evolves underneath you.

What you're signing up for

  • A genuinely unsolved problem — the constraint here is people and adoption, not model capability.

  • High agency. We set outcomes, not playbooks. You and your team define how this evolves.

  • Real commercial breadth. This team sits at the intersection of Product, go-to-market, and eligibility — closer to the customer than most engineering roles.

  • Craft that's respected, not traded off. Strict typing, layered testing, ADRs, observability — and AI-native ways of working as the baseline, not an experiment.

  • A company mid-transformation, told straight. Multiverse is rebuilding itself into a product-powered, AI-native company in real time. You're not inheriting a finished system — you're one of the people defining it.

What you'll do

You will own delivery, technical direction, and team health in the D&P service estate — the full learner and customer journey from diagnosis through prescription to onboarding and growth tracking. Concretely, that means leading the team(s) across surfaces like:

  • Diagnosis & needs assessment — AI-heavy services (retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), LLM-scored assessment) that turn raw signal into a picture of where a learner or employer actually is.

  • Prescription & eligibility — build the product which helps learners and customers understand the best learning course for their skills and career development, that leverages a customer's levy funds. Much of this is load-bearing logic with a genuine financial and regulatory blast radius.

  • Recommendation & onboarding — turning a diagnosis into the right prescribed path and getting learners into it, where those decisions become visible to customers and learners.

  • The platform arc — continuing to carve D&P logic out of the shared legacy monolith into dedicated services, while backing the newer AI-native product from beta toward scale.

  • Coach and build the team. Hire well, give every report a real growth plan, and move the team into a high-performing, AI-native operating rhythm — promotions and performance issues are never a surprise.

  • Stay hands-on. Whiteboard distributed designs, review and negotiate the RabbitMQ event schemas and API contracts that ripple across services, and write production code yourself when it's the fastest way to de-risk or unblock.

  • Deliver predictably. Use cycle time, change failure rate, and MTTR to balance shipping speed, debt, and change-safety on logic with genuine financial and regulatory blast radius.

  • Raise the AI-native bar. Prove better discovery-to-build-to-review loops on your own team and share what works across engineering.

  • Partner on strategy. Work directly with Product and Design — and closely with go-to-market — to turn learner and customer behaviour into technical direction on the surfaces where eligibility and recommendation decisions become visible to real customers.

What we need

A few terms you'll see below: D&P (Diagnose & Prescribe, this team's name), BAM (our hiring framework — Behaviour, Achievement, Mastery), ADRs (architecture decision records), IfATE (the UK body governing apprenticeship standards).

  • Engineering management of full-stack teams shipping production software, with real technical depth to review architecture and challenge design.

  • A team you led has shipped AI features to real users and operated them — not a side experiment.

  • Strong Python/TypeScript (if you don’t have Typescript, you will need to learn): React/Next.js (App Router, RSC, server actions), tRPC/GraphQL, Node/Express.

  • PostgreSQL at scale via an ORM, with migration discipline on large, live schemas.

  • Event-driven systems on a message bus (we use RabbitMQ) — versioned events, idempotency, backward-compatible migration.

  • A high engineering maturity bar as second nature: typing, testing, feature flags, ADRs, CI/CD, observability.

  • AI-native delivery in practice — you build daily with Claude Code, Cursor, or the current best tool, and understand context management, model selection, tool design, and the token economics that separate a prototype from an affordable production system.

What sets you apart

  • GTM/acquisition-funnel experience — you've owned surfaces where onboarding and eligibility meet real customers.

  • Strangler-pattern pragmatism — legacy monolith and greenfield edge-native product, at the same time.

  • Accessibility and UX as defaults on learner-facing surfaces, not afterthoughts.

Not for you if

This role won't fit if you'd rather run ceremonies than stay in the system, the design, and the code yourself. It also won't fit if you see AI tooling as a productivity tweak rather than a step change in how a team works. And it needs someone who renegotiates the scope out loud when it's wrong, not someone who absorbs it and hopes it works out.

Stack & how we lead

TypeScript core (React/Next.js, Node) with PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ as the event backbone, plus Python and Elixir services — from RAG pipelines to a Claude-powered edge-native product. GitHub, CircleCI, Datadog. AI-assisted development is first-class, not bolted on.

You'll lead full-stack engineers (with Python/Elixir specialists), report to the Senior Director of Engineering for Diagnose & Prescribe, and calibrate regularly with a peer group of EMs — you're not doing this alone. We reject micro-management: we set the objective, you and your team own the how. Kindness, candour, and curiosity over hierarchy — bad news travels as fast as good.

Benefits

  • Time off: 27 days holiday (including 3 winter shutdown days) and bank holidays, plus 5 extra days off (1 life event, 2 volunteer days and 2 summer shutdown days).

  • Health and wellbeing: Bupa private medical insurance, a medical cash back plan, therapy through Spill and gym access through Wellhub.

  • Equity for all: we believe that when Multiverse wins, we all win, which is why every permanent employee receives share options.

  • Financial security: life insurance at 3x salary, a workplace pension with 4% contribution from us, Cycle to Work and a Tech Scheme.

  • Family support: enhanced maternity and paternity leave, adoption and shared parental leave, paid leave after pregnancy loss, and a workplace nursery scheme.

  • Hybrid working: 3 days a week in the office - except for Coaches & Instructors who come into the office 1 day per month. Plus 10 days a year to work from anywhere.

  • Work perks: quarterly team socials, company-wide events, happy hours, lunch delivered to the office once a week, fully stocked snack bar and a drinks fridge!


Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy, our Prevent Policy and all other Multiverse company policies. Successful applicants will be required to undertake at least a Basic check via the Disclosure Barring Service (DBS).

For roles that will involve a Regulated Activity, successful applicants must also undergo an Enhanced DBS check, including a Children’s Barred List check and a Prohibition Order check. Roles involving Regulated Activity may interact with vulnerable groups, therefore are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 meaning applicants are required to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings.

Providing false information is an offence and could result in the application being rejected or summary dismissal if the applicant has been selected, and possible referral to the police and the DBS.

title: Senior AI Product Manager - Mobile Experience
descriptionHtml:

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior AI Product Manager to join our Mobile Experience team. Our apps are where customers live with us day to day - recording trips, seeing their driving rating, managing their policy and getting help. For most of our customers, the app is Zego.

You’ll own a product domain within our apps, defining its quarterly strategy and goals and helping shape the longer-term direction of the Mobile Experience. You’ll lead discovery and delivery across iOS and Android, and use AI both to move faster and to build smarter experiences.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define your domain’s quarterly strategy and goals, and help refine the longer-term plans for the Mobile Experience.

  • Lead complex discovery autonomously, from customer research and design partnerships to opportunity solution trees and business cases.

  • Craft mobile experiences customers prefer, from effortless onboarding to intuitive self-serve, that also cost less to serve.

  • Validate before you build, using A/B tests, feature flags, staged rollouts and rapid prototypes to back or kill ideas early.

  • Ship at pace in reusable building blocks across iOS and Android, working with engineering, design, data and compliance.

  • Put the right metrics in place, from adoption and retention to app ratings and stability, and use them to drive continuous improvement.

  • Establish AI-enabled workflows for your domain, and explore AI-powered experiences inside the app.

  • Bring stakeholders along, running ceremonies with senior stakeholders, facilitating big-room planning and knowing when to escalate.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

title: Senior Avionics Hardware Certification Engineer (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
As a Senior Hardware Certification Engineer with focus on DO-254, you will be an important part of our Certification and Systems Engineering organization, supporting the development and certification of advanced unmanned aircraft systems.

Your main focus will be the development assurance and certification of airborne electronic hardware. You will work closely with Hardware, Systems Engineering, Safety, Verification & Validation and Certification teams to ensure that hardware development and verification activities fulfil the applicable certification objectives.

You will translate certification and safety requirements into practical engineering activities and help ensure that the required compliance evidence is complete, consistent, traceable and ready for review by certification authorities.

What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Plan, coordinate and support DO-254 / ED-80 hardware certification activities throughout the hardware development lifecycle.

  • Develop, review and maintain certification artefacts such as the Plan for Hardware Aspects of Certification (PHAC), Hardware Verification Plan (HVP), Hardware Configuration Management Plan (HCMP), Hardware Accomplishment Summary (HAS) and supporting compliance evidence.

  • Define and maintain DO-254 compliance matrices and ensure that applicable objectives are addressed by appropriate engineering evidence.

  • Support determination and justification of the applicable Hardware Design Assurance Level (DAL) together with Systems and Safety Engineering.

  • Ensure bidirectional requirements traceability between system requirements, hardware requirements, design data and verification evidence.

  • Review hardware requirements, conceptual and detailed designs, verification activities and lifecycle data against DO-254 objectives.

  • Define and review hardware verification methods, test cases, procedures, analyses and results, including the required level of independence.

  • Work closely with Hardware Development, Systems Engineering, Safety, Test & Verification and Configuration Management to integrate certification activities into the engineering lifecycle.

  • Support certification reviews, audits and authority engagements and provide clear technical justification for the selected means of compliance.


What you bring to the team:

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering or a comparable technical discipline.

  • Professional experience in airborne electronic hardware development, hardware verification, aerospace certification or development assurance.

  • Strong practical knowledge of RTCA DO-254 / EUROCAE ED-80 and its application to airborne electronic hardware.

  • Experience with hardware certification planning, requirements management, verification and compliance evidence.

  • Good understanding of FPGA / CPLD or complex electronic hardware development, electronic hardware and PCB development, hardware requirements and design reviews, requirements-based verification, configuration management, change control, requirements traceability, verification independence, and COTS or reused hardware assessment.

  • Experience creating or reviewing DO-254 lifecycle documents such as PHAC, HVP, HCMP and HAS is highly desirable.

  • Familiarity with AC 20-152A or comparable authority guidance for airborne electronic hardware is an advantage.

  • Knowledge of related aerospace development and safety standards such as ARP4754A, ARP4761 / ARP4761A and DO-178C is advantageous.

  • Experience working with aviation certification authorities or within a DOA or military airworthiness environment is advantageous.

  • Structured and analytical working style with a strong focus on traceability, evidence and technical correctness.

  • Ability to communicate complex certification requirements effectively to hardware engineers and other engineering disciplines.

  • Fluent English, written and spoken. German language skills are beneficial.

Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you dont meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.

Why Quantum-Systems:

  • We believe in the power of combined efforts: straightforward tech expertise paired with a customer-centric focus.

  • We are industry pioneers who are ambitious, bold, and visionary.

  • We push limits, think outside-the-box and strive for technological excellence to shape the future of aerial data.

  • We promise to be your runway for individual and professional growth.

Our benefits:

  • Company pension scheme: We support you so that you can already make provisions for later.

  • Flexible working hours: With trust-based working hours, you are not only responsible for your working hours, but also for your work-life balance.

  • Mobile Work: If things get a little busy in the office, you have the option to work remotely one flexible day per week to create the right balance.

  • Stay active: With EGYM Wellpass, you get access to thousands of fitness and sports facilities — and of course, we subsidize the membership.

  • Bike-Leasing: We support you in staying environmentally mobile and healthy.

  • Corporate Benefits: Your opportunity for attractive offers and discounts from well-known suppliers and brands, e.g. Adidas, Apple, Expedia.

  • Employee events: We not only want to grow together, but also celebrate our successes together.

  • Lunch-Card: Be powerful with delicious energy, daily lunch budget is sponsored.

  • Company Shuttle: Enjoy our convenient shuttle service that picks you up from Laim in Munich and brings you to our location, with return trips at the end of the workday.

About us:

Quantum Systems is a leading European deep-tech company for unmanned systems across air, land and maritime domains. We develop and scale integrated hardware, software and AI-powered solutions for mission-critical operations. By combining autonomous platforms with intelligent software and AI, Quantum Systems enables customers to operate, understand and act across domains.

title: Senior Cloud Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Security Team 👋

At Trainline, security is embedded into everything we build. Our team partners closely with Engineering to design, implement and continuously improve the controls that keep our platforms, customers and services secure. Working across Cloud Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, Platform Engineering and the wider security function, we help embed security into every stage of the technology lifecycle while supporting innovation at scale.

As a Senior Cloud Security Engineer, you’ll take ownership of how we protect the cloud platforms that power digital journeys for millions of customers. You’ll set direction for our cloud security approach, shape how we respond to emerging risks, and act as a trusted voice across Engineering, GRC and Privacy as we strengthen our security posture and keep pace with a constantly evolving technology landscape.

In this role as the Senior Cloud Security Engineer, you will...🚄

  • Own and continually evolve the security controls across our AWS cloud environment, setting the standard for secure-by-design principles across networking, infrastructure and identity management.

  • Lead collaboration with Cloud Engineering, Platform and DevOps teams to secure containerised workloads using technologies such as Docker and Amazon ECS/Fargate, driving down vulnerabilities and raising the bar for compliance through automation.

  • Drive the strategy behind our Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) tooling, ideally Wiz, identifying cloud misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and security risks, and holding Engineering teams accountable for timely remediation.

  • Take the lead in identifying, prioritising and resolving complex security issues within cloud environments, guiding teams towards secure, resilient service design.

  • Build and maintain strong partnerships with Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) and Privacy teams, ensuring cloud security controls align with regulatory, compliance and data protection requirements.

  • Shape the development of cloud security policies, standards and controls, ensuring alignment with recognised frameworks including CIS Benchmarks, NIST and SOC 2.

  • Champion the integration of security into CI/CD pipelines and software delivery processes, driving automation, vulnerability management, AI-assisted tooling and security testing across the organisation.

  • Act as a senior point of contact during cloud security incidents, leading detection, investigation and remediation activities while championing a security-first mindset across Trainline.

We’d love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • Significant experience implementing and owning security controls within AWS environments, with a strong understanding of AWS native security services and best practices.

  • Experience using Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) solutions, ideally Wiz, to identify and drive remediation of cloud misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and security risks.

  • A strong understanding of cloud networking concepts, including VPCs, subnets, security groups and network ACLs, with experience of technologies such as Content Delivery Networks (CDNs), Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) and DDoS protection services including AWS Shield.

  • Experience working with source control platforms such as GitHub or GitLab.

  • Significant experience with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or AWS CloudFormation, and a solid understanding of how infrastructure automation supports secure cloud environments at scale.

  • A track record of partnering with Engineering, GRC and Privacy teams to embed security into cloud services, with the confidence to influence stakeholders on compliance and risk management decisions.

  • Experience automating security controls and operational workflows using modern tooling, ideally with exposure to AI-assisted capabilities to improve efficiency and reduce manual effort.

  • A collaborative and pragmatic approach, with strong communication skills and the confidence to shape security practices and influence decision-making across the organisation.

More information:

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

  • 🤝  Travel Together - We're one team 

  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

title: (Senior) Content Producer (Mensch) für unseren Kunden Google
descriptionHtml:
About WPP Media

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships – all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. 

WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.

For more information, visit wppmedia.com.

EssenceMediacom ist eine neue Art von Medienagentur und eine der führenden Marken der WPP Media. Auf der Grundlage von Analysen und Erkenntnissen und angetrieben durch Daten und Technologie glauben wir an die Kraft von Medien und Kreativität, um den besten Marken der Welt zum Durchbruch zu verhelfen. Wir sind für die neue Kommunikationswirtschaft konzipiert - für Menschen und Algorithmen, mit unterschiedlichen Denkansätzen, um in großem Maßstab zu testen und zu lernen, und vor allem, um sich weiterzuentwickeln. 

Das bieten wir dir:

  • Work-Life-Balance: Dank flexibler Arbeitszeiten mit Schwerpunkt auf dem persönlichen Austausch im Office und ergänzender Remote Work passt sich dein Job deinem Leben an. Überstunden kannst du flexibel ausgleichen.
  • Vacation mode on: Du erhältst 30 Urlaubstage plus einen flexiblen Tag – zusätzlich sind der 24. und 31.12. frei.
  • Wellbeing first: Gesundheitsleistungen, attraktive Altersvorsorge sowie Mental Health Awareness Days stellen deine Gesundheit in den Mittelpunkt.
  • Practice makes perfect: Entfalte dich mit unseren vielfältigen Weiterbildungen und nutze unsere internen Karriereprogramme für deine Entwicklung im WPP-Netzwerk.
  • More than just a job: Dich erwarten unvergessliche Events, Mitarbeitendenrabatte und weitere Highlights wie das Job Ticket, Wellhub oder das Job Bike.
  • Be yourself: Bei uns ist jede:r herzlich willkommen - Vielfalt und Chancengleichheit liegen uns am Herzen.

Das bewegst du:

Als (Senior) Content Producer (Mensch) in unserem Content & Partnership Team bist du das operative Rückgrat für die Aussteuerung komplexer Content-Produktionen und Media-Partnerschaften, dediziert für unseren Kunden Google. Mit einem starken Social-First-Fokus, einer agilen Hands-on-Mentalität und höchstem Qualitätsanspruch an eine flawless execution sorgst du dafür, dass freigegebene Konzepte wirksam und mit lokaler Relevanz im deutschen Markt zum Leben erweckt werden.

  • Projektplanung & Agilität: Souverän übersetzt du komplexe Briefings und Media-Partnerschaften in detaillierte Produktionspläne, leitest Kick-offs sowie wöchentliche Status-Calls und hältst interne wie externe Beteiligte verlässlich auf Kurs.
  • End-to-End-Produktionssteuerung: Du verantwortest die operative Umsetzung komplexer Video-, Content- und Event-Produktionen, von der Planung über die professionelle Koordination und Aussteuerung vor Ort am Set bzw. beim Dreh bis hin zur finalen Auslieferung.
  • Social-First & Media Delivery: Du prüfst Deliverables gewissenhaft auf Qualität (QA) und stellst sicher, dass alle Assets – insbesondere Social-First-Formate – exakt den technischen Spezifikationen der jeweiligen Plattformen und Media-Owner entsprechen.
  • Stakeholder Management: Als zentraler Knotenpunkt zwischen Kunde, Media-Teams und externen Partnern baust du vertrauensvolle Beziehungen auf, prüfst die produktionstechnische Machbarkeit von Ideen und moderierst operative Zielkonflikte stets lösungsorientiert.
  • Mentoring & Teamführung: Du teilst dein Know-how aktiv im Team, bringst dich in die Optimierung unserer Workflows ein und unterstützt bei der Einarbeitung sowie, je nach Erfahrungslevel, als fachliche:r Mentor:in für weniger erfahrene Kolleg:innen (z. B. auf Junior-Level).
  • Digitale Innovation & KI: Mit Begeisterung für technologische Weiterentwicklung evaluierst du den gezielten Einsatz von KI-Tools in Produktions-Workflows und befähigst das Team, diese effizient im Alltag zu nutzen.

Das zeichnet dich aus:

  • Erfahrung: Du bringst mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung als Content Producer in einer integrierten Agentur, einem Media-Netzwerk oder bei einem Publisher mit und hast einen klaren Track Record in der Steuerung von Media-Partnerschaften und Digitalkampagnen.
  • Operative Exzellenz: Du besitzt herausragende Projektmanagement-Fähigkeiten, bringst Struktur in anspruchsvolle Prozesse und behältst auch in dynamischen Phasen stets einen kühlen Kopf.
  • Social-First- & Produktionswissen: Du hast ein tiefes Verständnis für die Content-Produktion digitaler Assets und Creator-Workflows; Mediapläne musst du nicht selbst schreiben, kannst sie aber fehlerfrei lesen, verstehen und produktionstechnisch ableiten.
  • Plattform-Expertise: Du kennst die Spezifikationen moderner Kanäle und Plattformen (Social-First, interaktive Formate, DOOH) aus dem Effeff und stellst eine nahtlose Einbindung aller Assets in die Media-Landschaft sicher.
  • Kundenorientierung: Du überzeugst durch Kommunikationsstärke im Umgang mit anspruchsvollen Stakeholdern und fühlst dich im schnellen Takt eines globalen Tech-Umfelds wohl.
  • Sprachkompetenz: Verhandlungssicheres Englisch in Wort und Schrift (unsere tägliche Geschäftssprache im internationalen Austausch) sowie sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse für die lokale Marktumsetzung.
  • Reisebereitschaft: Du begleitest Produktionen und Events zuverlässig vor Ort und bringst eine entsprechende Reisebereitschaft für Dreh- und Produktionstage mit.

Darüber hinaus bist du: #agil #strukturiert #qualitätsbewusst 

Wenn du diesen Job spannend findest, dann ermutigen wir dich ausdrücklich zur Bewerbung, auch wenn du nicht jede oben gelistete Qualifikation aufweisen kannst.

Arbeiten bei WPP Media:

Als WPP Media gestalten wir die Zukunft der Medien und investieren dabei konsequent in unsere Mitarbeiter:innen. Jede:r Kolleg:in genießt die Vorteile des globalen Netzwerks von WPP Media und WPP, um sich weiterzuentwickeln und an der Spitze von Marketing und Werbung zu lernen. Vielfalt und Zusammenhalt leben wir durch zahlreiche Employee Resource Groups und regelmäßige interne Events - zum Austausch, zur Inspiration und zum gemeinsamen Feiern unserer Erfolge.
 
WPP Media ist ein Arbeitgeber, der Chancengleichheit fördert. Wir berücksichtigen alle Bewerber:innen für alle Positionen ohne Diskriminierung. Unser Ziel ist eine Kultur des Respekts und der Zugehörigkeit, in der jede:r die gleichen Möglichkeiten hat, sich einzubringen und beruflich zu wachsen.

title: Senior Content & Search Activation Lead
descriptionHtml:
Established in 2004, OLIVER is the world's first and only specialist in designing, building, and running bespoke in-house agencies and marketing ecosystems for brands. We partner with over 300 clients in 40+ countries and counting. Our unique model drives creativity and efficiency, allowing us to deliver tailored solutions that resonate deeply with audiences.

As a part of The Brandtech Group, we're at the forefront of leveraging cutting-edge AI technology to revolutionise how we create and deliver work. Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results.

Role: Senior Content & Search Activation Lead (6 Month-FTC)

Location: London, or Northampton, England (3 days a week on-site from our Client's offices)

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a six-month contract opportunity to join OLIVER'S managed services team, embedded within our client, a leading & Global Banking Institution. Sitting within their Marketing Centre of Excellence as a Senior Content & AI Search Specialist, you'll be responsible for turning search, GEO and audience insight into live content and customer experiences across priority journeys.

Based in London or Northampton, with a hybrid working pattern (three days a week on-site), you'll take insight from specialist agency partners and turn it into approved, delivery-ready content and digital briefs, working with delivery teams to get activity live. Your judgement and writing will help the Unified Search programme improve how customers find and use our client's content.

About the role:

This is a hybrid activation role that combines content strategy, SEO, copywriting, campaign management and stakeholder management. Rather than being the primary source of search insight, you'll add value by translating specialist recommendations into clear, prioritised and deliverable activity. Your value is in taking recommendations from partners such as OMD and Profound, checking them against the Unified Search strategy, and shaping them into clear, prioritised activity.

You'll secure the right approvals and work with Delivery Managers and Digital Delivery teams to move work into delivery. You'll use AI-enabled tools and workflows, such as Profound and Pencil Pro, to speed up briefing and content creation, while applying careful human judgement.

You'll help build confidence in the Supercharge model by keeping recommendations moving from insight to approval, delivery and post-live learning. You'll work across a matrix of Product, Content, Design, Digital Delivery, Legal, Compliance and agency partners, with no direct reports.

What you will be doing:

  • Move search, GEO and content recommendations from agency insight or content brief through to deployment-ready activity.
  • Review recommendations from OMD, Profound and other insight sources, and confirm they fit the Unified Search strategy, customer journey priorities and sprint objectives.
  • Work with Product stakeholders, including product owners, to secure alignment and sign-off before activity moves into delivery.
  • Use Profound, Pencil Pro and other AI-enabled workflows to shape content, write briefs, develop copy and optimise pages.
  • Write, edit and refine copy and messaging where needed, turning recommendations into clear and usable content outputs.
  • Work with the assigned Delivery Manager to translate recommendations into clear content, optimisation and digital delivery requirements.
  • Check with Content, Design, Digital Delivery and agency partners that requirements are clear, prioritised and complete before handover.
  • Prepare opportunities for the relevant sign-off board and coordinate stakeholder input where approval is needed.
  • Maintain a visible backlog for your area or sprint wave, so recommendations are prioritised, progressed and tracked.
  • Decide whether to progress, pause, re-scope or escalate an opportunity, based on risk, dependency and delivery readiness.
  • Flag blockers, dependencies and governance issues early, and escalate them clearly through the Supercharge operating model.
  • Make sure all content aligns with our client's brand, tone of voice, accessibility, legal, compliance and risk requirements.
  • Feed live performance results and learnings back into future sprint activity.
  • Risk and Control Objective: Ensure that all activities and duties are carried out in full compliance with regulatory requirements, Enterprise-Wide Risk Management Framework and our clients' internal Policies and Policy Standards.

What you need to be great in this role:

  • Experience across financial services or a heavily regulated industry
  • Experience in content strategy, content design, copywriting or digital content.
  • A good understanding of SEO principles, including search intent, page structure, metadata, internal linking, content quality and customer journey optimisation.
  • Understanding of GEO and AI search principles, or a strong appetite and ability to learn quickly.
  • Experience reviewing, writing or refining digital content, and turning recommendations into actionable briefs.
  • Skill in using insight, customer need and search data to shape practical content and optimisation activity.
  • Stakeholder management experience with Product, Content, Design, Digital, Legal, Compliance or agency teams.
  • Experience taking work through approval, governance or delivery processes in a regulated environment.
  • Organisational skills, including managing backlogs, priorities and actions, and keeping work moving through ambiguity and competing priorities.
  • Clear communication, including explaining search and content recommendations to non-specialist stakeholders.
  • Experience applying sound judgement and working within appropriate risk, legal, compliance and governance controls.
  • Confidence using Gen AI tools to improve the quality and speed of content, briefing and optimisation activity.
  • An ability to adopt and help embed repeatable AI-assisted content and briefing workflows.
  • A systematic approach to breaking down complex, multi-step challenges.
  • Sound judgement about where AI can add value and where human review, specialist expertise and governance are required.

The Problems You'll Solve

The Problems You'll Solve

About You

  • Commercially minded and client-focused. You communicate legal advice crisply and concisely, building strong relationships with sophisticated financial services clients.

At Carta, you're not just an employee. You're a builder who is creating infrastructure that accelerates innovation and empowers more ownership.
