title: Working Student – Hardware Engineering (UAS Propulsion & Power) (All Genders)
descriptionHtml:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

WHY JOIN US

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

ABOUT THE TEAM

You will join our hardware engineering team, working closely with engineers across propulsion, power systems, testing, and aircraft development to turn measured data into better-performing unmanned systems.

YOUR MISSION

Your mission is to work hands-on with the parts of the aircraft that turn stored energy into flight: the
motors, the batteries, and the propulsion and power components that decide how far, how fast, and how
long our platforms fly. You support the hardware team from bench characterisation through data analysis
in MATLAB and Python.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK

  • Support characterisation and bench testing of motors, propellers, batteries, and power components for our UAS platforms.
  • Help set up test rigs and instrumentation, and capture clean, repeatable measurement data.
  • Assist with component selection and trade-offs by turning test data into clear comparisons.
  • Reduce and analyse test data in MATLAB and Python — efficiency, thrust, endurance, thermal and discharge behaviour.
  • Visualise results so the engineering team can make decisions from them quickly.
  • Keep test setups, measurements, and findings documented and traceable.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION

  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace, or a comparable engineering field.
  • Working knowledge of MATLAB and Python for data analysis.
  • Interest in and some exposure to UAS, electric propulsion (motors / ESCs), or battery / power systems.
  • Must be a citizen of a NATO member state (due to export control and security regulations).
  • Practical, hands-on mindset — comfortable at the bench and with a multimeter as much as in a script.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English; German is a plus.
  • Hands-on: You like building, measuring, and finding out what really happens.
  • Rigorous: You trust clean measurements over assumptions.
  • Curious: You want to understand why a component behaves the way it does.

NICE TO HAVE

descriptionHtml:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

ABOUT THE TEAM

We are a cross-functional engineering team powering our Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems (C-UAS) program. Built on the background of the Minerva Edge CTRL team, our engineers create onboard edge software and integrated systems across core STARK platforms, delivering dependable performance when timing and accuracy matter most. Today, we are building the next-generation stack and physical integration for the STARK C-UAS platform at the intersection of hardware, real-time embedded systems, computer vision, and AI-driven navigation.

As a Drone Engineer Working Student for Dragonfly, your mission is to bring our autonomous C-UAS systems to life in the physical world. Serving as a vital link between hardware development and software execution, you will assemble and refine our aerial platforms, design mechanical and electrical solutions, and build critical testing environments.

title: Workplace Technology Lead

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

As the Workplace Technology Lead you'll be the domain expert and technical authority for workplace technology and AV innovation within Corporate Engineering. Setting technical direction, leading technology delivery for capital builds, and creating and owning repeatable standards that support employees, clinicians and members.

This is a senior technical leadership role, so you'll deliver by influencing, coordinating and partnering across the organisation (Engineering, Facilities, Clinical, Real Estate). It combines hands-on delivery, programme leadership and practical AI solutions, and you'll shape how the function grows as Neko expands.

Your scope covers collaboration and meeting spaces, employee experience, executive briefing centres, clinic environmental AV and debrief-room presentation, digital signage, and technology integration across a growing portfolio of health centres. Network, security, facilities, clinical systems and scanning hardware stay with their specialist owners, and you'll work closely with them.

  • Map the estate, opening pipeline, suppliers, ownership and risks in your first 60 days, and agree the role charter, roadmap and budget baseline with Technology and Operations

  • Create a global technology roadmap aligned to expansion plans, workplace needs and the member experience, turned into investment priorities, delivery plans and lifecycle budgets

  • Act as design authority for workplace and AV: define reference designs, preferred solutions and a clear process for local variations

  • Review existing standards, take full ownership of them in Corporate Engineering, and create a repeatable technology build playbook, piloted on an agreed site or room type

  • Lead the technology workstream for new offices, health centres and refurbishments, from feasibility and design through procurement, commissioning and operational handover

  • Own the integrated technology programme: financial forecasts, risks, changes and executive reporting, with clear readiness criteria, acceptance tests and defect tracking for each opening

  • Work with clinical operations and design teams on debrief displays, ambient audio, signage and controls, prioritising simple use, discretion and a calm environment for members

  • Test two approved operational AI use cases, for example automated commissioning tools, through measured pilots

  • Establish asset and lifecycle records, supplier reviews and service requirements with Procurement and support owners

What We're Looking For

  • Experience taking technology projects through architectural design, procurement, construction, commissioning and handover, with commercial and programme accountability

  • Ability to explain technical decisions to executives, clinicians, designers and delivery partners, and to connect investment choices to practical user needs
